text:
elaine: quick rally re cross-project service auth. core idea: central minting broker issues short-lived signed tokens that include service id + origin project. targets verify locally with cached public keys. default deny for cross-project; target must opt in via whitelist. thoughts?
sam: 👍. must carry both `sub=svc:name` and `origin=proj:xxx`. billing+audit use origin, policy uses both.
hassan: revocation: don't want per-request introspection. propose signed tokens + revocation stream (pubsub) to edge caches. use revocation bloom + sliding window.
nick: TTL tiers: sensitive scopes 2m-5m, normal 15m-60m. fallback if broker unreachable: allow emergency cached certs but only readonly scopes and explicit project opt-in.
audit-bot: audit must log token_id, sub, origin, policy_result, verifier_key_id, and raw token claims. append-only store, 90d retention.
ops-bot: deploy pipelines need a mint API; we'll add client libs and retry/backoff patterns.
elaine: mapping idea: scopes -> roles + allowed_projects. example: `call:write` -> role write-exec with allowed_projects [proj-A]. policy pseudo: `if token.origin != target.project and not whitelisted deny; roles = map(scopes); check roles`.
sam: rotation: broker keys rotate daily with overlap; verification caches poll jwk endpoint and handle grace window.
hassan: migration: identify non-human long-lived keys, require migration in 180d; block cross-project use after 90d.
elaine: next: I'll draft RFC covering token schema, TTL tiers, revocation stream, whitelist UX, SLA. @sam @hassan volunteer to review.
sam: happy to review.
hassan: will draft revocation streaming design.
elaine: thanks — opening RFC issue now. :rocket:
